title: The Field Trip Mix-Up
summary: Two students accidentally board the wrong group's bus on a museum field trip and learn to stay calm and ask a teacher for help instead of panicking.
poll: When something goes wrong on a trip, staying calm and finding an adult is the best first step.

versions.title: The Field Trip Mix-Up
versions.text:
Yousef and Noura go on a trip. They go to a museum. The class splits into two groups.

The trip ends. The friends talk and laugh. They do not look at the buses. They make a mistake and get on the wrong bus.

The bus is full of kids they do not know. Yousef feels worried. Noura feels worried too.

Noura takes a breath. She tells Yousef to stay calm. They do not shout.

They see a teacher at the front. She is not their teacher. She can still help. They talk to her in a calm voice.

The teacher is kind. She calls their teacher. Their own teacher comes fast.

Yousef and Noura get on the right bus. Their teacher is glad. She says staying calm was smart.

versions.title: The Field Trip Mix-Up
versions.text:

The bus is full of kids they do not know. Yousef feels a jump of worry. Noura feels worried too. For a second, she almost wants to shout.

Instead, Noura takes a slow breath. She quietly tells Yousef to stay calm. The two friends agree not to panic.

They notice a teacher near the front. She is not their own teacher. But she is still able to help them. They explain the mix-up in a calm voice.

The kind teacher listens and calls their own teacher. Within a few minutes, their teacher arrives at the bus.

Yousef and Noura happily move to the right bus. Their teacher says she is proud, because staying calm was the right thing to do.

versions.title: The Field Trip Mix-Up

Yousef and Noura are thrilled to go on a trip to a city museum. Their class is split into two groups. Each group has its own bus.

After a fun morning, the two friends walk outside together. They are still chatting and laughing about everything they saw. They do not look closely at the row of buses. By mistake, they climb onto the wrong one.

The bus is full of kids they do not recognize. Yousef feels an uncomfortable jump of worry. Noura feels worried too. For a second, she almost wants to shout.

Instead of panicking, Noura takes a slow breath. She quietly tells Yousef that they need to stay calm. The two friends agree not to panic.

They notice an unfamiliar teacher near the front. She is not their own teacher. But she is still able to help them. They calmly explain the mix-up.

The kind teacher listens patiently and calls their own teacher. Within a few minutes, their teacher arrives at the bus, looking relieved.

Yousef and Noura happily move to the right bus. Their teacher tells them how proud she is, because staying calm and asking for help was the right thing to do.

versions.title: The Field Trip Mix-Up
versions.text:
On a bright Thursday, Yousef and Noura's class heads out for a field trip to a city museum. Before the buses leave, the teachers split the class into two groups. Each group gets its own bus for the day.

The museum visit is fascinating. There are old artifacts and a dinosaur skeleton that almost touches the ceiling. By the time the two friends head back outside, they are still chatting about what they saw. They do not pay close attention to the row of buses. They climb aboard the wrong one.

It quickly becomes clear that something is wrong. The bus is full of unfamiliar faces, students who do not recognize Yousef or Noura either. A jolt of worry rises in Yousef's chest, and for one second, Noura feels an urge to shout at their confusing predicament.

Instead, Noura takes a slow breath. She quietly reminds Yousef that panicking will not help. The two friends agree that staying calm is their best option.

Scanning the bus, they spot an unfamiliar teacher near the front. She is not their own teacher, but she is still a responsible adult who can help. They walk calmly toward her and explain what happened in a steady voice.

The teacher listens, then calmly calls their own teacher. Within a few minutes, their teacher arrives, relieved to find them safe.

Back on the right bus, Yousef and Noura receive warm praise. Their teacher explains to the class that staying calm and asking for help, rather than panicking, was exactly the right way to handle a confusing moment.

keyWords.definition: a building where people go to see interesting old or special things
keyWords.example: We saw an old ship model at the museum.
I made a mistake and wrote the wrong date on my paper.

keyWords.definition: quiet and not worried or upset
keyWords.example: She stayed calm even when she dropped her lunch tray.

keyWords.definition: feeling afraid that something bad might happen
keyWords.example: He felt worried when he could not find his backpack.

keyWords.definition: a person whose job is to help students learn
keyWords.example: Our teacher read us a story after lunch.

questions.stem: What is this story mostly about?
options: Two friends who end up on the wrong school bus
Two friends who get lost at a park
A class that builds a museum at school
A teacher who gets lost on the way to school
questions.why: The story is about Yousef and Noura getting on the wrong bus by mistake and staying calm until a teacher helps them.

wrong.B: The story is about a bus, not a park.
wrong.C: The class visits a museum but does not build one.
wrong.D: The teacher on the bus is not lost.

questions.stem: Why do Yousef and Noura get on the wrong bus?
options: A teacher tells them to get on it
Their own bus breaks down
They are talking and miss the bus
They want to sit with new friends
questions.why: The story says they are chatting and laughing, so they do not look closely and climb on the wrong bus by mistake.

wrong.A: No teacher tells them to board that bus.
wrong.B: The story does not say the bus breaks down.
wrong.D: They do not plan to sit with new friends; it is a mistake.

questions.stem: What happens right after they realize they are on the wrong bus?

They call their parents on a phone
They fall asleep right away on the bus
They feel worried but choose to stay calm

wrong.A: They do not jump off; the bus may already be moving.
wrong.B: They do not use a phone; the teacher does.
wrong.C: They do not fall asleep in the story.

questions.stem: In the story, a mix-up means —
options: a fun game played at the museum
a confusing mistake
a kind of bus seat
a snack eaten on the trip

wrong.A: A mix-up is not a game.
wrong.C: A mix-up is not a type of seat.
wrong.D: A mix-up is not a snack.

questions.stem: Why do Yousef and Noura talk to the teacher on the bus?

To ask her for a snack
To tell her about the museum
Because she asked them to sit down

wrong.C: They talk to her about the mix-up, not the museum.
wrong.D: She does not tell them to sit down.

questions.stem: What can you tell about Noura from the story?

She does not like going to museums
She can stay calm in a hard moment
She does not want to find her teacher

wrong.B: She seems to enjoy the museum trip.
wrong.D: She wants to find a teacher to help them.

To show that she is angry at Yousef

To show that she is calming herself down

LOW.prompt: What would you do if you got on the wrong bus like Yousef and Noura? Use at least two facts from the story in your answer.
checklist: I clearly said what I would do.
I used at least two facts from the story.
I wrote complete sentences with capital letters and periods.
LOW.modelAnswer: If I got on the wrong bus, I would try to stay calm like Noura did. I would not shout, even if I felt worried inside. I would look for a teacher on the bus, because a teacher can help fix the mix-up. I would explain what happened in a calm voice, just like Yousef and Noura did.

keyWords.definition: to know someone or something because you have seen it before

keyWords.definition: able to be trusted to do what is right or needed

keyWords.definition: feeling glad and less worried because a problem is solved

wrong.A: Calling parents is not mentioned in the story.
wrong.B: She does not hide under her seat.
wrong.C: She does not ask the driver to turn the bus around.

questions.stem: Why are Yousef and Noura able to recognize that something has gone wrong?
options: The bus is completely full of unfamiliar faces
The bus driver tells them they are on the wrong bus
A sign on the bus says it belongs to another school
The museum guard stops them from boarding
questions.why: Seeing that the bus is full of students they do not recognize is what tips them off that they boarded the wrong one.

wrong.B: The bus driver does not tell them this.
wrong.C: No sign is mentioned in the story.
wrong.D: No museum guard appears in the story.

questions.stem: In the story, the word responsible describes the unfamiliar teacher because she —
options: is in charge of driving the bus herself on the trip
can be trusted to help solve the students' problem
designed the museum's dinosaur exhibit last year
wrote the field trip permission form for the class
questions.why: The teacher is described as responsible because, even though she is unfamiliar, she can be trusted to help the two students.

wrong.A: The teacher is not described as driving the bus.
wrong.C: The exhibit design is not mentioned.
wrong.D: The permission form is not mentioned in the story.

questions.stem: Why do Yousef and Noura choose to approach the unfamiliar teacher instead of panicking on their own?
options: They believe she is secretly their own teacher in disguise
They want to ask her for a snack
They think she will let them skip the museum next time
They know an adult can help solve the problem calmly
questions.why: The story shows the two friends reasoning that a trustworthy adult can help fix the mix-up better than panicking alone.

wrong.A: The story makes clear she is simply a different, unfamiliar teacher.
wrong.B: A snack is never mentioned.
wrong.C: Skipping future museum trips is not mentioned.

questions.stem: How does the author organize the events of the story?
options: By describing the mix-up and then the calm resolution
By comparing two different museums in detail
By listing rules for riding a school bus safely
By explaining the life story of the unfamiliar teacher
questions.why: The story first presents the mix-up, then shows the students staying calm and seeking help, and ends with the teacher's arrival and praise.

wrong.B: Only one museum is described in the story.
wrong.C: The story is not a list of bus safety rules.
wrong.D: The teacher's personal history is not explained.

questions.stem: How are Yousef's and Noura's reactions to the mix-up alike, even though they each feel a brief urge to react differently?
options: They both ultimately choose to stay calm instead of panicking
They both decide to get off the bus immediately, in a panic
They both blame the bus driver for the mistake, and shout at him
They both refuse to talk to the unfamiliar teacher on the bus
questions.why: Although both feel a flash of worry, Yousef and Noura each end up agreeing, without much discussion, to remain calm.

wrong.B: Getting off the bus is not what they decide to do.
wrong.C: Neither friend blames the bus driver in the story.
wrong.D: They do talk to the unfamiliar teacher, calmly.

MID.prompt: Explain how Yousef and Noura handle the problem of being on the wrong bus. Use at least two details from the story.
checklist: I explained the problem and how the characters solved it.
I used at least two details from the story.
I organized my ideas in a clear order.
MID.modelAnswer: Yousef and Noura accidentally board the wrong bus because they are distracted by conversation and do not look closely at the buses outside the museum. When they realize the bus is full of unfamiliar faces, they both feel a flash of worry, but Noura takes a slow breath and reminds Yousef that panicking will not help. Instead of shouting, they calmly approach an unfamiliar teacher near the front of the bus and explain the mix-up. The teacher calls their homeroom teacher, who arrives within minutes and praises the two friends for staying calm and asking for help.

keyWords.definition: a short trip taken for pleasure or education
keyWords.example: The school organized an excursion to the science center.

keyWords.definition: done in a careful, thoughtful way, not by accident
keyWords.example: He took a deliberate step back before answering the difficult question.

keyWords.definition: calm and in control of one's feelings, especially under pressure
keyWords.example: The young singer remained composed even after forgetting a line on stage.

keyWords.definition: to find a solution to a problem or disagreement
keyWords.example: The two neighbors met to resolve their argument about the fence.

keyWords.definition: to expect something and prepare for it before it happens
keyWords.example: The coach anticipated rain and packed extra towels for the team.

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses the central idea of the story?
options: Staying calm and finding a responsible adult resolves this mix-up quickly.
A field trip is canceled because students repeatedly fail to follow instructions.
A museum guide becomes lost while leading two students through an exhibit.
Two students compete to see who can find their own bus first.
questions.why: The story's main point is that Yousef and Noura's composed, sensible response to their mix-up, seeking out a trustworthy adult, leads to a quick resolution.

wrong.B: No field trip is canceled in the story.
wrong.C: No museum guide becomes lost; the mix-up involves buses, not a guide.
wrong.D: The two friends cooperate rather than compete.

questions.stem: What specifically causes Yousef and Noura to board the wrong bus?
options: They deliberately choose to sit with unfamiliar students
A teacher mistakenly directs them onto the wrong bus
Their own bus is unexpectedly out of service that day
They stay absorbed in talk and miss the row of buses
questions.why: The story explains that the two friends are so absorbed in excited conversation that they do not notice the buses closely, leading to the mix-up.

wrong.A: Their boarding is accidental, not deliberate.
wrong.B: No teacher directs them onto the wrong bus.

questions.stem: What deliberate action does Noura take to keep herself and Yousef from panicking?
options: She searches every seat on the bus for an exit
She texts her parents for instructions
She takes a slow breath before speaking to Yousef
She asks the bus driver to stop immediately
questions.why: The story specifically describes Noura taking a slow, deliberate breath before calmly addressing the situation with Yousef.

wrong.A: Searching for an exit is not described.
wrong.B: Texting parents is not mentioned.
wrong.D: She does not ask the driver to stop.

questions.stem: In the story, the word anticipate most closely relates to which idea?
options: The students had been looking forward to and expecting an enjoyable trip
The students were completely surprised that a field trip existed at all
The teacher failed to expect any problems with the bus arrangement
The museum anticipated that students would misbehave
questions.why: The story says the students had been anticipating the trip for weeks, meaning they expected and looked forward to it.

wrong.B: They clearly knew about and expected the trip in advance.
wrong.C: The teacher's expectations about problems are not the focus of the word's use here.
wrong.D: The museum's expectations about behavior are not mentioned.

questions.stem: Based on the story, why do the two friends approach the unfamiliar teacher rather than trying to resolve the situation entirely on their own?
options: They know a responsible adult can contact their teacher and resolve it
They are required by school rules to speak only to unfamiliar adults
They hope the teacher will let them skip the rest of the field trip
They mistakenly believe she already knows their own teacher personally
questions.why: The story implies that the two friends recognize an adult can contact their teacher directly, resolving the predicament more efficiently than they could alone.

wrong.B: No such school rule is mentioned.
wrong.C: Skipping the rest of the trip is not their goal.
wrong.D: Nothing suggests they believe the teacher already knows their own teacher.

questions.stem: In what order do these events occur in the story?
options: The teacher calls their homeroom teacher, the friends board the wrong bus, Noura takes a breath
The friends board the wrong bus, Noura takes a breath, the teacher calls their homeroom teacher
Noura takes a breath, the friends board the wrong bus, the teacher calls their homeroom teacher
Their teacher arrives, the friends board the wrong bus, Noura takes a breath
questions.why: The friends first board the wrong bus by mistake, then Noura calms herself and Yousef, and only afterward does the unfamiliar teacher call their homeroom teacher.

wrong.A: The teacher cannot call before the friends even board the wrong bus.
wrong.C: Noura's calming breath happens after boarding the wrong bus, not before.
wrong.D: Their teacher arrives at the very end, after the call is made.

questions.stem: What can readers infer from Yousef's "small, uncomfortable jolt of anxiety" upon realizing the mix-up?
options: He is genuinely excited about meeting new students
He is annoyed that the museum trip has ended too early
He feels an instinctive worry about the unfamiliar situation
He suspects that Noura has caused the mix-up on purpose
questions.why: A jolt of anxiety suggests an instinctive, uncomfortable reaction of worry to the sudden realization of their confusing situation.

wrong.A: The reaction described is worry, not excitement.
wrong.B: The end of the museum visit is not what troubles him.
wrong.D: Nothing suggests he blames Noura for the mix-up.

questions.stem: Why does the author end the story with the teacher explaining the lesson to the entire class?
options: To show that staying composed and finding a responsible adult is the right response
To describe in detail how school buses are scheduled each morning
To suggest that only Yousef and Noura learned anything from the experience
To introduce an entirely new problem the class must now resolve
questions.why: The teacher's closing explanation reinforces the story's broader lesson about composure and seeking help during a confusing predicament.

wrong.B: Bus scheduling details are not the story's focus.
wrong.C: The lesson is shared with the entire class, not just the two friends.
wrong.D: The story resolves its problem; it does not introduce a new one.

HIGH.prompt: The poll says that when something goes wrong on a trip, staying calm and finding an adult is the best first step. Do you agree or disagree? Support your argument with evidence from the story about Yousef and Noura's predicament.
checklist: I stated a clear position on the poll statement.
I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that staying calm and finding an adult is the best first step when something goes wrong on a trip. In the story, Yousef and Noura accidentally board the wrong bus and are surrounded by unfamiliar students, yet instead of panicking, Noura takes a deliberate breath and the two friends calmly approach an unfamiliar teacher, who quickly resolves the mix-up by contacting their own teacher. Someone might argue that it would be faster to simply get off the bus and search for the right one alone, but doing so in an unfamiliar place could easily make the predicament worse; approaching a responsible adult, as Yousef and Noura did, led to a safe and remarkably quick resolution.
